_about: PRO batch 50: the cross-era pool, set A.

scenarios.title: Packing Up the House
scenarios.text: The new contract is in {town}. Your friends, your routines and your favorite diner are all where you live now, and the moving company has sent a quote that is mostly zeros.

choices.label: Move everyone together
choices.result: Everything moves to {town} at once, boxes and plants and all. It's a hard month of unpacking alone, and the new place has a bigger yard, which helps more than you expected.

choices.label: Go alone for the season
choices.result: You go alone for the season and fly home every bye week, while {sibling} checks on the house. It's lonely and practical, and the nightly calls get longer as the weeks go by.

choices.label: Bring {parent} for the first month
choices.result: {parent} comes with you for the first month to help you settle in. Together you find the grocery store, the good bakery and a dentist, and the new city stops feeling foreign.

scenarios.title: The Family Stays Behind
scenarios.text: You'll be in {town} during the season, and your family will be a flight away. {sibling}'s kids have drawn you a calendar with every visit marked in a different color of crayon.

choices.label: Fly home every off day
choices.result: A flight home on every off day, even for a single night. You're tired all season, your legs feel the travel, and you never miss a birthday or a school play.

choices.label: Call every night at seven
choices.result: Seven o'clock, every night, on video, with homework help and bedtime stories, and {parent} filling in on the nights you can't. The kids set alarms for it.

choices.label: Bring them for a month
choices.result: The whole family comes to {town} for a month in the middle of the season. The apartment is crowded and loud and wonderful, and the kids learn every song the crowd sings.

scenarios.title: Your Old Team Comes to Town
scenarios.text: Your old club is on the schedule this week. Half their locker room still texts you, the equipment manager sent a care package, and the reporters want a revenge story.

choices.label: Visit their locker room
choices.result: You visit their locker room before warmups to hug the equipment manager and the snapper. It feels like a reunion, not a revenge, and you leave with a bag of their candy.

choices.label: Give the reporters nothing
choices.result: No revenge story and no quotes, just kicking. The reporters write that you were 'gracious', which is fine, and the week passes without a single headline about you.

choices.label: Let yourself want it
choices.result: For once you let yourself want it. Every kick in practice that week has a little extra in it, and you sleep badly, replaying old meetings you thought you'd forgotten.

scenarios.title: The Tryout Hotel
scenarios.text: You got the job at a Tuesday tryout. Now you live in a hotel by the airport until somebody says otherwise, with a suitcase, a kicking bag and a room-service menu you've memorized.

choices.label: Make the hotel a home
choices.result: A plant, a photo, a rented bike and a favorite diner down the road. It's a strange little home with planes overhead, and it keeps you steady through the uncertain weeks.

choices.label: Live at the facility
choices.result: You're at the facility all day, every day: film, gym, kicks. You only go back to the hotel to sleep, and you're the best-prepared player in the building by October.

choices.label: Find a teammate to share with
choices.result: A teammate with a spare room offers it by the second week. Real dinners, real conversation, and a friend for the season instead of a menu and a television.

scenarios.title: Family Asks for Money
scenarios.text: {sibling} needs money, a real amount, and doesn't want {parent} to know. They call late, after the kids are asleep, and apologize three times before they say the number.

choices.label: Help, and keep the secret
choices.result: You send the money quietly and keep the secret. {sibling} pays you back slowly over two years, a little every month, and never forgets that you didn't ask any questions.

choices.label: Help, with a plan
choices.result: You help, with conditions: an advisor, a budget, a plan written down. {sibling} grumbles and agrees, and it works well enough that they never need to call you like that again.

choices.label: Ask them to tell {parent}
choices.result: You gently ask them to tell {parent}. They do, eventually, after a hard week, and the family solves it together, slowly, around the same table where all the big things get solved.

scenarios.title: The Recital
scenarios.text: A school recital, a road trip, and a kid who has asked you three times if you'll be there. The recital starts at seven; the team plane leaves at five.

choices.label: Ask to fly separately
choices.result: You arrange a late flight with {coach}. You're in the second row at seven and on a plane at ten, and your kid waves at you from the stage halfway through the song.

choices.label: Watch on a video call
choices.result: From the team plane, over spotty wifi, you watch on your phone and the whole specialist unit crowding the screen. They all clap at the end, and {holder} asks for an encore.

choices.label: Make it up after
choices.result: A promise, kept, and a private recital at home when you get back. Your kid performs it for you twice, in full costume, and {parent} films both shows on an old phone.

scenarios.title: Your Partner's Career
scenarios.text: Your partner has been offered the job of a lifetime, in a city with no team, four hours away. They're trying hard not to look excited, and failing completely.

choices.label: Tell them to take it
choices.result: You tell them to take it, and you mean it. The next year is complicated and full of flights and missed dinners, and they've never been happier, which makes it worth it.

choices.label: Plan it together
choices.result: A plan made together on a whiteboard: weekends, the offseason, a house halfway. It's hard and it holds, because you built it together, and {best_friend} helps you move the first boxes.

choices.label: Ask them to wait a season
choices.result: You ask them to wait one more season. They agree, and something goes quiet between you that takes a long time to come back, even after the season ends.

scenarios.title: The Old Friend's Ticket Requests
scenarios.text: {best_friend} asks for tickets every single week and brings a different stranger every time. This week's stranger wants a photo in the locker room with the whole specialist unit.

choices.label: Keep saying yes
choices.result: You keep saying yes, every week, because it's {best_friend}. The strangers are mostly nice, one of them makes everyone laugh for an hour, and one of them becomes a real friend.

choices.label: Set a limit
choices.result: Two games a month, you tell {best_friend} kindly over the phone. They laugh, agree, and start bringing better strangers, and your locker room stops feeling like a tourist stop.

choices.label: Invite {best_friend} alone
choices.result: Just {best_friend} this time, no strangers, and a long dinner after the game. It's the best night you've had together in a year, full of old stories you'd both forgotten.

scenarios.title: A Teammate in Trouble
scenarios.text: A teammate's arrest is on every channel. He calls you from his lawyer's office and asks you to speak for his character at the hearing next week.

choices.label: Speak honestly
choices.result: At the hearing you speak honestly: what you've seen of him, no more and no less. The judge listens carefully, and so does your teammate, who thanks you afterwards in the hallway.

choices.label: Help him find better help
choices.result: You find him a better lawyer and a counselor through the union. It isn't what he asked for, and it's the help he actually needed, which he admits a month later.

choices.label: Decline politely
choices.result: You say no, kindly, because you don't know enough about what happened. He's hurt and hangs up quickly, and weeks later he tells you he understands, though things stay a little cooler.

scenarios.title: The Tabloid
scenarios.text: A gossip site prints a story about your marriage that's mostly made up: a fight in a restaurant that never happened, a quote from a 'friend' you've never met.

choices.label: Ignore it together
choices.result: You ignore it together at the kitchen table, with the laptop firmly closed. It's gone in a week, and you laugh for months about the mysterious 'friend' who knows you so well.

choices.label: Have your lawyer respond
choices.result: A letter from your lawyer and a quiet correction a week later on page nine. Few people see it, and that's fine, because the people who matter already knew the truth.

choices.label: Joke about it publicly
choices.result: A joke at your locker about the restaurant you've never been to. The story turns into a punchline, the teammates start making reservations there, and the site quietly deletes the piece.

scenarios.title: The Marriage on the Road
scenarios.text: You've been home eleven nights since August, and your partner has stopped asking when you'll be back. The house runs perfectly without you, which is exactly the problem.

choices.label: Talk about it tonight
choices.result: Tonight, on the phone, for two hours: everything, including the part that scares you both. It doesn't fix anything yet, and it's the honest start of fixing it.

choices.label: Plan real time together
choices.result: Real time, planned: the bye week, the offseason, and one night a week with no phones while {parent} keeps an eye on the house. It helps, slowly, and you both stop counting the nights.

choices.label: Push through to the offseason
choices.result: Through to the offseason, you tell yourself, and you pour everything into kicking instead. The distance at home grows another inch, and you can feel it in every short call.

scenarios.title: The Locker Room Fight
scenarios.text: Two starters are swinging at each other by the cold tub over something nobody can remember, and the rookies are all looking at you to see what happens next.

choices.label: Step between them
choices.result: You step between them calmly, hands up, talking the whole time. It stops, and both of them apologize to you afterwards, which is strange, and the rookies remember it all season.

choices.label: Get the coaches
choices.result: You fetch the coaches fast. It's over in a minute, nobody gets hurt, and the rookies see how a room is supposed to work when something breaks, which matters more than they know.

choices.label: Talk to both of them later
choices.result: You talk to both of them separately that evening, over dinner and over the phone. By Friday they're joking again, and nobody knows you had anything to do with it.

scenarios.title: The Labor Fight
scenarios.text: The league and the union are fighting over the next agreement, and the owners are talking about replacement players. As your team's union rep, the young players want answers from you.

choices.label: Hold a players' meeting
choices.result: A meeting with the facts and none of the rumors, questions welcome. The young players leave calmer than they came in, and the room holds together through a long, tense month.

choices.label: Learn every detail
choices.result: You learn the whole proposal in detail, every clause, so every answer you give is right. It's dull, late-night work, and it's the most important thing you do all spring.

choices.label: Talk to the veterans first
choices.result: You consult the veterans first, one by one, so the room speaks with one voice. It takes longer than anyone wants, and it works when the vote finally comes.
